sections.title: Context
paragraphs: The plot sits on Gudamendi, in Igeldo, 180 m above the sea. The sea keeps temperatures regular, there is little shade and a steady wind, and sewage, water, power, phone and a bus stop are close. The main façade faces south to limit winter heat loss.

sections.title: Envelope
paragraphs: Stone on the ground floor resists rain splash; vertical timber cladding above. An asymmetric pitched roof in ventilated zinc, which is abundant, lasts a century and is endlessly recyclable. Triple glazing with two chambers, low-emissivity glass and micro-slat blinds; cellulose insulation made from recycled paper, recovering the old paper mills of the river Oria.

sections.title: Energy systems
paragraphs: My part. Hybrid PV-thermal panels on the steep south slope preheat domestic hot water and make electricity for lighting, devices and the heat pump. A small wind turbine works from 10 m/s. Surplus energy is stored in batteries in the attic and the rest goes to the grid. The heat pump heats through the floor, finishes the hot water and reverses for cooling in summer.

sections.title: Water
paragraphs: The shallow roof slope collects rainwater into an underground tank used for the washing machine, toilets and garden irrigation.
